subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu direct session can become unusable after /reset or /new and fall back to generic 'Something went wrong...' while session index points to missing transcript IDs

question: For direct chat `/reset` and `/new`, should OpenClaw publish the new session id only after creating a durable transcript header, or should it keep the previous transcript authoritative until the first successful write?
rationale: Current source shows the durable-lineage invariant is not fully proven, but the exact recovery semantics affect session continuity, cleanup, and user-facing error copy across channels.

options.title: Pre-create Before Publish
options.body: Create the new transcript header before committing the new session entry, and roll back to the previous entry if creation fails.

options.title: Keep Old Until First Write
options.body: Leave the previous transcript mapped until the next turn successfully writes the new transcript, avoiding orphan ids at the cost of delayed rotation semantics.

options.title: Repair Only
options.body: Rely on cleanup/doctor repair plus clearer failure copy, which is lower risk to runtime flow but leaves live recovery weaker.

recommendation.title: Pre-create Before Publish
recommendation.body: Create the new transcript header before committing the new session entry, and roll back to the previous entry if creation fails.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and Feishu/session repair history make this the best available routing owner for the reset/new durability decision.
